title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Manufacturing
description: Curated OT/ICS cybersecurity advisories, incidents and threat intelligence from primary sources. Editorial summaries by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

_otthreatfeed.usage: Free to reuse with attribution. Credit 'Mike Holcomb & UtilSec' and link back to otthreatfeed.com and to each item's linked primary source. Summaries are editorial paraphrase - verify against the primary source before acting.

items.title: Dragos counted 1,140 industrial ransomware incidents in Q2 — and not one reached stage 2 of the ICS kill chain
items.content_text: Dragos’s Q2 2026 industrial ransomware analysis recorded 1,140 incidents against industrial organisations, up 12% on Q1. Manufacturing absorbed 747 of them (65%), led by construction at 176 and equipment manufacturing at 114; food and beverage accounted for 70. The finding worth carrying into your own risk conversations is the negative one: Dragos found no case in Q2 where a ransomware operator reached stage 2 of the ICS Cyber Kill Chain. Production stopped because enterprise IT and ERP systems stopped — order entry, scheduling, shipping, labelling — not because anyone touched a controller. Named Q2 cases include West Pharmaceutical Services and Foxconn, the latter with a roughly two-week outage at Wisconsin and Texas sites. That pattern should shape where you spend: the loss is real, but the control is IT/OT dependency mapping and recovery, not deeper controller hardening.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Dragos Q2 2026 Industrial Ransomware Analysis — via Help Net Security

items.title: Analog Devices disclosed data exfiltration in an SEC filing; an extortion group claims 570,000 records
items.content_text: Semiconductor maker Analog Devices disclosed unauthorised system access and data exfiltration in a 30 July 2026 SEC filing, having discovered the intrusion on 23 June 2026, and stated it does not expect a material business impact. The ExfilSquad group claimed responsibility for over 570,000 stolen customer records; the company has neither confirmed nor denied that claim, so treat the volume figure as claimed rather than established. Semiconductor manufacturers sit far enough upstream that a compromise there is a supply-chain concern for everyone downstream — not because fabs are likely to be sabotaged, but because customer, design and roadmap data concentrates in a small number of organisations.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Analog Devices SEC filing — via The Record

items.title: Coca-Cola’s Fairlife suspended all US dairy production after a ransomware attack
items.content_text: Coca-Cola’s Fairlife dairy subsidiary suspended all US production on 16 July 2026 following a ransomware attack on production-related systems, disclosed via SEC filing. The company said product safety and quality were unaffected and engaged law enforcement and outside forensics. Whether attackers reached plant-floor control systems or only business IT was not confirmed at disclosure, and that distinction has not been publicly resolved. The Anubis ransomware group later claimed on its leak site to have locked Fairlife servers and stolen around 1 TB of data, with stolen VPN credentials cited as the suspected initial access; Coca-Cola has not confirmed the actor or the data theft, so treat the claim as unverified. Included as standing context — it is the reference case behind this month’s sector reporting.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Coca-Cola SEC filing — via Cybersecurity Dive

items.title: Attackers took hands-on control of water-utility PLCs across a dozen states — locking out operators and knocking a treatment plant offline
items.content_text: Between 26–27 July 2026 a coordinated campaign disrupted automated controls at more than 30 Minnesota community water systems, and confirmed intrusions have since been reported across roughly a dozen states including Georgia, Michigan, South Dakota, Alabama and New Jersey. This is hands-on manipulation of control equipment, not a data breach: CISA says the actors changed PLC passwords and altered device IP addresses to lock operators out of their own equipment. In Braham, Minnesota a pump failure forced a treatment facility offline and prompted a resident conservation notice; Clayton County, Georgia issued a precautionary boil-water advisory after a pump-station disruption, later lifted. Dragos’s Rob Lee told NPR he could not recall “this many targets at once with operational impact.” Every affected utility reported that drinking water stayed safe, with staff falling back to manual operation. Federal officials have pointed to Iran-linked activity — a TLP:AMBER WaterISAC assessment reportedly found the evidence aligned with campaigns previously attributed to Iran — but no formal public attribution has been made, so treat the actor as suspected rather than confirmed.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: CISA / FBI / EPA, MNIT and affected city statements — via NPR, The Record, Dark Reading, BleepingComputer
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Incidents from 26 Jul 2026; scope reporting through 12 Aug 2026

items.title: A CVSS 10.0 command injection in Haiwell’s cloud HMI gateway hands an unauthenticated attacker root
items.content_text: CISA advisory ICSA-26-225-02 covers CVE-2026-19188, an OS command injection (CWE-78) in the Haiwell IoT Cloud HMI Gateway that scores the full CVSS 10.0. The flaw sits in the device’s Net Check function: an unauthenticated attacker can reach the cmdPing Socket.io event and execute arbitrary commands as root. CISA flags the product’s use in energy, critical manufacturing and water/wastewater environments. Affected firmware is 3.40.1.12; the fix is 3.50.1.19. No in-the-wild exploitation had been reported at publication, which is the good news — a maximum-severity, unauthenticated, internet-reachable root execution on a gateway product is exactly the profile that gets weaponised quickly once someone bothers.

items.title: ABB Ability zenon ships an end-of-life MongoDB — and one of the 13 inherited CVEs is already being exploited
items.content_text: CISA advisory ICSA-26-218-01 bundles 13 vulnerabilities into ABB Ability zenon, all inherited from an outdated MongoDB 4.2 dependency shipped with the platform’s IIoT services. Scores run up to CVSS v3.1 7.5 / v4.0 8.7. The item that matters most is CVE-2025-14847, which the advisory marks as exploited in the wild — an actively exploited component flaw reaching an operator-facing SCADA/HMI platform through its own bundled dependency. Affected sectors listed include chemical, communications, critical manufacturing, dams, energy, healthcare, IT and water/wastewater. ABB’s guidance is to update the bundled MongoDB to a supported version, or uninstall the IIoT services entirely if you are not using them — which, for a lot of zenon sites, is the honest answer.

items.title: August ICS Patch Tuesday: a maximum-severity missing-authentication flaw in Siemens Simatic IoT2050, plus Schneider and Phoenix Contact fixes
items.content_text: Siemens published ten advisories in the August cycle. The headline item is a maximum-severity missing-authentication vulnerability in Simatic IoT2050 Advanced edge devices that a remote, unauthenticated attacker could use to execute code with elevated privileges. Also in the batch: an OS command injection in Siemens Siveillance Video / Milestone XProtect management servers (CVE-2026-3014, CVSS v3.1 9.1, v4.0 6.4) exploitable by users holding edit permissions, and two Siemens License Server flaws — CVE-2026-69108 (CVSS 6.0, local privilege escalation via an insecure sudoers policy) and CVE-2026-69109 (CVSS 7.5, path traversal), fixed in v5.1+ and v5.3+ respectively. Schneider Electric addressed two code/command execution issues in NetBotz 5 and an authentication-attempt flaw in PowerChute Serial Shutdown. Phoenix Contact published a PLCnext firmware advisory covering unauthenticated denial-of-service and malicious SQL query execution.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Siemens ProductCERT, Schneider Electric, Phoenix Contact — via SecurityWeek and CISA ICSA-26-225-07 / -09

items.title: AVEVA Enterprise SCADA deserialisation flaw could let tampered data become code execution
items.content_text: CISA advisory ICSA-26-225-01 covers CVE-2025-7639, a deserialisation-of-untrusted-data vulnerability in AVEVA Enterprise SCADA carrying CVSS v3.1 7.1. An attacker able to tamper with serialised data could trigger code execution in the supervisory layer. Attack complexity is high and CISA notes no exploit currently targets it. Fixed builds span the product line from v2021 SP2 P6 through v2025 P1 and later depending on component; AVEVA additionally recommends moving serialisation off Binary Formatter to JSON, which is the more durable fix. Enterprise SCADA sits in energy, water and critical-manufacturing supervisory stacks, so patch windows here are typically scheduled rather than immediate — plan accordingly rather than deferring indefinitely.

items.title: Cisco ASA and Firepower join KEV under active exploitation — the OT perimeter is the target again
items.content_text: CISA added CVE-2026-20349, a heap-inspection vulnerability in Cisco Secure Firewall ASA and Firepower Threat Defense software, to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 11 August 2026, citing evidence of active exploitation. The same batch added CVE-2026-68820, a use-after-free in the Windows afd.sys driver enabling local privilege escalation — relevant because Windows engineering workstations and HMI servers are exactly where that gets chained after initial access — and CVE-2026-72898, a SQL injection in Metabase exposing stored credentials. Earlier in the month CISA added CVE-2026-8037, an unauthenticated command injection in Progress Kemp LoadMaster carrying CVSS 9.6, after sustained exploitation attempts, with a federal patch deadline of 10 August under BOD 26-04. None of these are ICS products. All of them sit in front of, or inside, the path into OT.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: CISA KEV catalogue — via The Hacker News, CyberExperts

items.title: An N-able N-central auth bypass was exploited, patched incompletely, then exploited again
items.content_text: CISA added two N-able N-central authentication-bypass flaws to KEV within two days: CVE-2026-18556 and CVE-2026-18577, both CVSS 8.2, the second being an incomplete-fix follow-on to the first. N-able confirmed a limited number of customer breaches. Attackers who exploit it take over administrator accounts and can pivot to managed endpoints through the platform’s Take Control remote-session feature. Huntress reported that 55.6% of reachable cloud servers were still unpatched at the time of its analysis. The fix is 2026.3.1.7 / 2026.3 HF1. RMM platforms matter disproportionately in OT because they are how integrators, machine builders and managed-service providers reach plant equipment — often through a path that was never security-reviewed and does not appear on the network diagram.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: CISA KEV; N-able advisory — via The Hacker News, Help Net Security

items.title: A hardcoded key in Acrisure KARR anti-theft units means compromising one device exposes the fleet
items.content_text: CISA advisory ICSA-26-216-01 covers a hard-coded cryptographic key (CWE-321) in Acrisure’s KARR BT and DR-100 vehicle anti-theft and telematics units, tracked as CVE-2026-18411 with CVSS 8.1 per corroborating reporting. An attacker within Bluetooth range can unlock doors or engage immobilisation without authenticating. Because the key is shared across units rather than per-device, compromising one unit exposes every unit that ships with it — the defining property of hardcoded-secret flaws and the reason they are worth more attention than their individual scores suggest. Firmware dated 20 July 2026 or later resolves it. No public exploitation had been reported at publication.

items.title: Johnson Controls patched hardcoded credentials in the TL280 communicator and cross-site scripting in Metasys UI
items.content_text: Two Johnson Controls advisories landed in the August cycle. ICSA-26-218-02 covers CVE-2026-27871, hardcoded credentials in the TL280 internet security alarm communicator on firmware below 5.63, which could expose sensitive device data; CISA scores it CVSS v3.1 4.1 / v4.0 2.1 and notes high attack complexity. ICSA-26-225-14 covers a cross-site scripting weakness in the Metasys UI building-automation front end. CISA also issued Update A to its earlier advisory for C-CURE 9000 and victor application servers. Neither individual flaw is dramatic. The reason they belong on an OT page is placement: building automation, access control and alarm communications routinely share network segments with industrial systems while sitting outside the OT patching programme and often outside the OT asset register entirely.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: CISA ICSA-26-218-02, ICSA-26-225-14, ICSA-26-204-01 Update A

items.title: A 2024 truck-brake recall quietly fixed remote code execution — and none of it got a CVE
items.content_text: Research presented at Black Hat USA 2026 showed that a 2024 safety recall of Bendix EC80 heavy-truck brake electronic control units, covering roughly 450,000 units across three OEMs, quietly fixed buffer-handling flaws enabling remote code execution and denial-of-service, a hardcoded password that disabled traction control, and memory-corruption crashes. None of the issues received CVE identifiers. Researchers demonstrated triggering the bugs via software-defined radio through diagnostic ports, halting CAN bus traffic and disabling ABS and steering assist. The security-relevant finding is the disclosure gap: a safety recall was used as the remediation channel, so the vulnerabilities never entered any vulnerability database, and no fleet operator scanning CVE feeds would ever have learned about them.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Black Hat USA 2026 research — via SecurityWeek

items.title: Researchers found 4,407 internet-facing Rockwell controllers — and 19 of 22 in already-attacked cities ran firmware vulnerable to a 2017 bug
items.content_text: A Cloud Security Alliance scan on 3 August 2026 identified 4,407 internet-facing Rockwell / Allen-Bradley controllers worldwide, 2,844 of them in the United States. The more uncomfortable finding is local: of 22 exposed controllers located in cities already hit by the July campaign, 19 were still running firmware vulnerable to CVE-2017-16740, a buffer-overflow flaw patched back in 2017. Separately, CISA Acting Director Nick Andersen said federal responders assisting with the recovery are still finding water-system PLCs reachable from the internet with factory-default credentials or no password at all. Broader counts cited during the response put roughly 10,000 Rockwell, Siemens and Schneider devices on the public internet sector-wide. The takeaway is not a novel zero-day; it is that a decade of unpatched, unauthenticated exposure is doing the work for the attacker.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Cloud Security Alliance research note; CISA remarks via Nextgov/FCW

items.title: The federal PLC advisory grew beyond Rockwell — Schneider Modicon and Siemens S7-1200 are now named too
items.content_text: CISA, the FBI, EPA and NSA updated joint advisory AA26-097A on Iran-affiliated exploitation of internet-exposed programmable logic controllers, widening the documented target set from Rockwell MicroLogix and CompactLogix to also include Schneider Electric Modicon M340 / BMX P34 and Siemens S7-1200 devices. The update adds July 2026 indicators of compromise, the MITRE ATT&CK exfiltration technique T1041, and detection guidance for malicious modification of reusable Rockwell Add-On Instruction code blocks — the logic building blocks that water-treatment and other process programs are assembled from. The advisory names energy and government facilities alongside water and wastewater as targeted sectors. It is the foundational document behind the multistate water-utility incidents, and the detection guidance is worth reading even if you run none of the three named vendors.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: CISA joint advisory AA26-097A (CISA, FBI, EPA, NSA) — via WaterISAC
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Advisory updated 22 Jul 2026; originally issued Apr 2026

items.title: The OT Cybersecurity Coalition asked Congress to fix the plumbing behind critical-infrastructure threat sharing
items.content_text: Prompted largely by the water-sector attacks, the OT Cybersecurity Coalition — executive director Tatyana Bolton, chair Alison King of Forescout — called on Congress to confirm a director for the Department of Energy’s Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security and Emergency Response, reauthorise the State and Local Cybersecurity Grant Program, and extend the Cybersecurity Information Sharing Act of 2015, which expires in September 2026. The 2015 Act is the liability protection that makes many private-sector operators willing to share indicators with the government at all; if it lapses, the flow of the information this dashboard depends on gets thinner. Presented factually: these are the mechanisms currently under review, and their status affects operators regardless of position on the underlying policy.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: OT Cybersecurity Coalition — via Cybersecurity Dive
